title: How Do You Know It Went In?

scenes.tts: In chapter one, a stretch of the protein's own chain worked as an address. How do you know a protein really went inside? And how do you prove which stretch sent it?
scenes.caption: In chapter one, a stretch of the protein's own chain worked as an address. How do you know a protein really went inside? And how do you prove which stretch sent it?
scenes.narration: In chapter one, a stretch of the protein's own chain worked as an address. How do you know a protein really went inside? And how do you prove which stretch sent it?
scenes.visual: Open on chapter 1's world, so the pair reads as one film: dark cytosol, the GREY ribosome (two lobes, about 45% of frame height) at centre-left, a WHITE bead chain with its GOLD address beads leading, the INDIGO ER band along the bottom, the ORANGE mitochondrion at the right edge, the small MAGENTA peroxisome top-left, faint specks drifting. Same colour map as chapter 1: GOLD = address/signal; TEAL = SRP; BLUE = readers that wait elsewhere; INDIGO = ER membrane; ORANGE = mitochondrion; MAGENTA = peroxisome; RED = 'blocked' and cutting. New in this chapter: LIME = protease (a chomping cartoon cutter), CYAN = detergent (soap bubbles). On 'went inside', the GOLD-led chain threads into the ER band and a WHITE '?' pops beside the lumen. On 'which stretch', the GOLD beads pulse and a second WHITE '?' appears beside them. The persistent bottom-right label 'schematic, not to scale' returns and stays all film.

Title 'How Do You Know It Went In?' fades in across the top for 2 s and fades out. Behind it the camera starts pulling back: the cytosol world shrinks into the round bottom of a large glass TEST TUBE, which becomes the world for the first half.

scenes.tts: Start with the classic test. Make the protein in a test tube that also holds microsomes, sealed vesicles of E R membrane. Then add a protease, an enzyme that chews up exposed protein.
scenes.caption: Start with the classic test. Make the protein in a test tube that also holds microsomes, sealed vesicles of ER membrane. Then add a protease, an enzyme that chews up exposed protein.
scenes.narration: Start with the classic test. Make the protein in a test tube that also holds microsomes, sealed vesicles of ER membrane. Then add a protease, an enzyme that chews up exposed protein.
scenes.visual: THE TEST-TUBE WORLD (kept until s09): a tall glass tube fills the left two-thirds of frame, its liquid a dark cytosol colour with drifting specks. Inside float four or five INDIGO rings (vesicles), each about 15% of frame height; on 'microsomes' an INDIGO label 'microsomes (ER vesicles)' snaps to one ring. A small GREY ribosome inside the tube makes WHITE chains with GOLD leading beads, then the completed chains settle. Right third of frame: a gel panel with three empty lanes labelled 'no protease', '+ protease', '+ protease + detergent'; it stays all half. Only on 'Then add a protease', after synthesis has stopped, a LIME pipette tip dips in from the top and releases several LIME chomping cutters labelled 'protease' that swim through the liquid.

scenes.tts: The added protease cannot cross an intact microsome membrane. A chain outside the vesicles is chewed up. A chain inside is shielded, so its band survives on the gel.
scenes.caption: The added protease cannot cross an intact microsome membrane. A chain outside the vesicles is chewed up. A chain inside is shielded, so its band survives on the gel.
scenes.narration: The added protease cannot cross an intact microsome membrane. A chain outside the vesicles is chewed up. A chain inside is shielded, so its band survives on the gel.
scenes.visual: Zoom so one INDIGO vesicle fills about 60% of frame height, with one WHITE chain coiled inside it and one WHITE chain drifting in the liquid outside. The LIME cutters bump the vesicle rim and bounce off (small RED 'X' where they touch: 'cannot cross intact microsome'). On 'chewed up', cutters reach the outside chain and it breaks into scattered beads that fade. On 'shielded', the vesicle rim glows INDIGO. On 'its band survives', a WHITE band drops into the gel's '+ protease' lane at the same height as a band in the 'no protease' lane. Avoid any processed-versus-unprocessed band sizes here: both chains are plain WHITE, no GOLD.

scenes.tts: But maybe that protein simply resists protease. So add a detergent, which dissolves membranes. If the band now vanishes, the membrane was the shield.
scenes.caption: But maybe that protein simply resists protease. So add a detergent, which dissolves membranes. If the band now vanishes, the membrane was the shield.
scenes.narration: But maybe that protein simply resists protease. So add a detergent, which dissolves membranes. If the band now vanishes, the membrane was the shield.
scenes.visual: Camera eases back to show the whole tube. On 'resists protease', the protected WHITE chain inside the vesicle briefly gets a WHITE '?' tag. On 'detergent', CYAN soap bubbles labelled 'detergent' rise through the tube; where they touch, the INDIGO rings wobble, break into short arcs and dissolve. The freed WHITE chain is reached by LIME cutters and breaks into fading beads. On 'band now vanishes', the gel's third lane ('+ protease + detergent') stays empty with a faint dotted outline where the band would be; a GREEN tick appears by the label 'membrane was the shield'.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-five, Blobel and Dobberstein tested an antibody light chain, a secreted protein. Globin, which stays in the cytosol, was made the same way. Which survives the protease?
scenes.caption: In 1975, Blobel and Dobberstein tested an antibody light chain, a secreted protein. Globin, which stays in the cytosol, was made the same way. Which survives the protease?
scenes.narration: In 1975, Blobel and Dobberstein tested an antibody light chain, a secreted protein. Globin, which stays in the cytosol, was made the same way. Which survives the protease?
scenes.visual: Reset the tube with fresh INDIGO vesicles. Two kinds of chain come off GREY ribosomes in the liquid: a WHITE chain with GOLD leading beads labelled 'light chain (secreted)', and an all-WHITE chain labelled 'globin (stays in cytosol)'. A small caption at the tube's base: 'Blobel and Dobberstein, 1975'. LIME cutters wait at the top of the tube, still. On 'Which survives', a question card in white, size 36, spans the top: 'Which survives the protease?'
Thinking pause. The question card stays. Both chains drift slowly near the vesicles; the LIME cutters hover at the top, barely bobbing; specks drift. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: The light chain came out trimmed and protected. That happened only when the vesicles were there while it was being made. Globin was not protected.
scenes.caption: The light chain came out trimmed and protected. That happened only when the vesicles were there while it was being made. Globin was not protected.
scenes.narration: The light chain came out trimmed and protected. That happened only when the vesicles were there while it was being made. Globin was not protected.
scenes.visual: The card fades. First show synthesis: a GREY ribosome docks on an INDIGO vesicle, and the light chain's GOLD beads lead the growing WHITE chain inside. The GOLD beads separate and fade (trimmed), translation ends, and the WHITE remainder coils inside. Only then do the LIME cutters swim down. The protected chain remains; on the gel a WHITE band lands in the '+ protease' lane, slightly LOWER than its precursor band in the 'no protease' lane, with a small label 'trimmed'. The completed globin chain remains outside, is chewed and fades; RED tag 'not protected'. On 'only when the vesicles were there', a small side panel replays a separate reaction: the light chain is completed first with no vesicles, vesicles are added afterwards, and then protease is added. The chain stays outside and is chewed (RED tag 'vesicles added later').

scenes.tts: The parts came from three species: rabbit ribosomes, dog membranes, and mouse messenger R N A. They still worked together. That ruled out a special secretory ribosome and supported an address in the growing protein.
scenes.caption: The parts came from three species: rabbit ribosomes, dog membranes, and mouse messenger RNA. They still worked together. That ruled out a special secretory ribosome and supported an address in the growing protein.
scenes.narration: The parts came from three species: rabbit ribosomes, dog membranes, and mouse messenger RNA. They still worked together. That ruled out a special secretory ribosome and supported an address in the growing protein.
scenes.visual: Three labelled cartoon icons slide in along the top of the tube, each linked by a thin line to its part: 'rabbit' to the GREY ribosome, 'dog' to an INDIGO vesicle, 'mouse' to a short WHITE messenger RNA strand feeding the ribosome. On 'worked together', the three lines brighten together and the light chain threads into a vesicle once more. On 'special secretory ribosome', a label 'special ribosome' appears beside the GREY ribosome and gets a RED strike. On 'address in the growing protein', the GOLD beads pulse and a GOLD label 'address: growing protein' snaps beside them.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea. A sorting claim needs two kinds of test. One shows the protein got in; the other shows what sent it.
scenes.caption: So here is the idea. A sorting claim needs two kinds of test. One shows the protein got in; the other shows what sent it.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea. A sorting claim needs two kinds of test. One shows the protein got in; the other shows what sent it.
scenes.visual: Two lines build at the top in white, one per clause: 'GOT IN? protection test' (INDIGO on 'protection') and 'WHAT SENT IT? move and delete' (GOLD on 'move and delete'). On 'one shows the protein got in', the tube, vesicles and gel shrink into a small inset in the top-left corner (kept until the end). On 'what sent it', the camera dives back into chapter 1's cytosol world: GREY ribosome, ORANGE mitochondrion right, MAGENTA peroxisome top-left, INDIGO ER band dimmed to 30%. The two lines shrink and park in the top-right corner for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: To find the address, there are two tests. Move a stretch onto a protein that stays in the cytosol. If that passenger moves too, the stretch is sufficient.
scenes.caption: To find the address, there are two tests. Move a stretch onto a protein that stays in the cytosol. If that passenger moves too, the stretch is sufficient.
scenes.narration: To find the address, there are two tests. Move a stretch onto a protein that stays in the cytosol. If that passenger moves too, the stretch is sufficient.
scenes.visual: THE CELL WORLD (kept to the end). A WHITE folded ball labelled 'passenger (cytosolic)' drifts in the cytosol. A short GOLD bead segment is lifted off another chain by a dotted arrow and clicks onto the ball's end ('move'). On 'moves too', a generic outlined compartment labelled 'target' appears and the GOLD-tagged passenger follows a dotted arrow until it is inside; do not imply any particular import machinery. On 'sufficient', a GOLD label 'sufficient' appears under the parked 'move and delete' line.

scenes.tts: Or delete the stretch from its own protein. If the protein is stranded in the cytosol, the stretch is necessary. Chapter one's mouse enzyme was the first kind.
scenes.caption: Or delete the stretch from its own protein. If the protein is stranded in the cytosol, the stretch is necessary. Chapter 1's mouse enzyme was the first kind.
scenes.narration: Or delete the stretch from its own protein. If the protein is stranded in the cytosol, the stretch is necessary. Chapter 1's mouse enzyme was the first kind.
scenes.visual: A WHITE chain with its GOLD segment sits by an organelle. On 'delete', a RED eraser sweeps across the GOLD beads; they vanish and the chain falls back into the cytosol and wanders aimlessly, never reaching an organelle (RED tag 'stranded'). On 'necessary', a GOLD label 'necessary' appears beside 'sufficient'. On 'mouse enzyme', a ghost of chapter 1's GREY block 'DHFR (mouse enzyme)' with its GOLD address flashes beside the mitochondrion with a small tag 'sufficiency test'.

scenes.tts: Yeast cytochrome oxidase four precursor's first fifty-three amino acids carried mouse D H F R into the matrix. Adding S K L to a bacterial enzyme's carboxyl end sent it into mammalian-cell peroxisomes.
scenes.caption: Yeast cytochrome oxidase IV precursor's first 53 amino acids carried mouse DHFR into the matrix. Adding SKL to a bacterial enzyme's carboxyl end sent it into mammalian-cell peroxisomes.
scenes.narration: Yeast cytochrome oxidase IV precursor's first 53 amino acids carried mouse DHFR into the matrix. Adding SKL to a bacterial enzyme's carboxyl end sent it into mammalian-cell peroxisomes.
scenes.visual: Left half: the GREY 'DHFR (mouse enzyme)' block with a GOLD bead segment labelled 'COXIV precursor: first 53' threads through BLUE TOM and BLUE TIM23 in the two ORANGE membranes into the mitochondrion's matrix, unravelling as in chapter 1; GREEN tick 'sufficient'. Right half, on 'S K L': a WHITE passenger icon labelled 'bacterial enzyme' gains a short GOLD tip 'SKL' at its carboxyl end; BLUE PEX5 clasps the tip and carries the enzyme to the MAGENTA peroxisome (crossing drawn as a soft blurred patch, as in chapter 1); GREEN tick 'sufficient'. Small caption: 'in mammalian cells'.

scenes.tts: Now the other test. Deleting luciferase's carboxyl tail, no more than twelve amino acids long, left it in the cytosol. A signal in that tail is necessary.
scenes.caption: Now the other test. Deleting luciferase's carboxyl tail, no more than 12 amino acids long, left it in the cytosol. A signal in that tail is necessary.
scenes.narration: Now the other test. Deleting luciferase's carboxyl tail, no more than 12 amino acids long, left it in the cytosol. A signal in that tail is necessary.
scenes.visual: A WHITE folded ball labelled 'luciferase' with a short GOLD tail drifts toward the MAGENTA peroxisome. Rewind: the RED eraser removes the GOLD tail (label 'tail signal: ≤12 amino acids'). The tailless ball drifts past BLUE PEX5, which does not clasp it, and it stays in the cytosol; RED tag 'stays in cytosol'. GOLD label 'necessary' pulses.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. Working for one passenger does not prove it works for every passenger. And S K L is picky. In luciferase, only a few swaps to similar amino acids kept it working.
scenes.caption: Two cautions. Working for one passenger does not prove it works for every passenger. And SKL is picky. In luciferase, only a few swaps to similar amino acids kept it working.
scenes.narration: Two cautions. Working for one passenger does not prove it works for every passenger. And SKL is picky. In luciferase, only a few swaps to similar amino acids kept it working.
scenes.visual: Left: the GOLD-tagged passenger from s10 succeeds (GREEN tick), while a second, different GREY passenger with the same GOLD tag gets a WHITE '?' instead of a tick (label 'one passenger is not every passenger'); do not show it failing. Right: the GOLD 'SKL' tip shown as three lettered blocks S, K, L; one block at a time flickers to a different letter; a few flickers keep a GREEN tick, most turn RED (label 'only a few swaps work', schematic).

scenes.tts: And when a protein carries two signals, only an experiment can say where it goes. Protection shows it got in; moving and deleting show what sent it.
scenes.caption: And when a protein carries two signals, only an experiment can say where it goes. Protection shows it got in; moving and deleting show what sent it.
scenes.narration: And when a protein carries two signals, only an experiment can say where it goes. Protection shows it got in; moving and deleting show what sent it.
scenes.visual: A WHITE chain carrying a GOLD amino-end segment and a GOLD carboxyl-end tip sits in the cytosol between the ORANGE mitochondrion and the MAGENTA peroxisome; two dotted arrows point to both, each with a WHITE '?' (do not resolve it). On 'only an experiment', the chain gets a WHITE tag 'test it'. On 'Protection shows', the tube inset in the top-left brightens and its vesicle glows INDIGO; on 'moving and deleting', the parked 'move and delete' line in the top-right brightens and the GOLD 'sufficient' and 'necessary' labels pulse.

End card on the dark ground: the exact take-home line 'Protection shows it got in; moving and deleting show what sent it.' is centred in white, size 40, with 'Protection' in INDIGO and 'moving and deleting' in GOLD. Behind it, faintly, one INDIGO vesicle with a WHITE chain inside slowly drifts while a LIME cutter bounces off its rim.
scenes.line: Protection shows it got in; moving and deleting show what sent it.
